children: Japanese rubber futures fell on Thursday, tracking a pullback in oil prices and weakening cost support as Thai raw material supply entered its seasonal increase.
The Osaka Exchange (OSE) rubber contract for April delivery
was down 2.1 yen, or 0.47%, at 444.5 yen ($2.82) per kg, as of 0149 GMT
The rubber contract on the Shanghai Futures Exchange (SHFE) for January delivery
fell 350 yuan, or 1.79%, to 19,215 yuan ($2,882.54) per metric ton
The most active December butadiene rubber contract on the SHFE (SHBRv1) rose 60 yuan, or 0.36%, to 16,785 yuan per metric ton

Benchmark US crude futures fell around $1 on Thursday, paring some of the previous day's gains, as traders weighed the risk that escalating Middle East conflict could further disrupt regional energy supplies
Natural rubber often takes direction from oil prices as it competes for market share with synthetic rubber, which is made from crude oil
Top producer Thailand's raw materials entered a seasonal increase in October, weakening cost support, said analysts from broker GF Futures in a note

The price of Thailand's benchmark export-grade smoked rubber sheet (RSS3) (RUB-RSS3C-BKK) and block rubber (RUB-STR20C-BKK) were down 0.02% and 1.58%, to stand at 95.73 baht per kg and 87.35 baht per kg, respectively

Cambodia's cumulative rubber exports reached 299,000 tons in the first eight months of 2026, up 11.6% from 268,000 tons a year earlier, with China, Singapore, Vietnam and Malaysia as the main destinations, data from rubber information provider Qinrex showed
The front-month rubber contract on Singapore Exchange's SICOM platform for January delivery (STFF7) last traded at 246.2 US cents per kg, down 1.42%
